arcs.title: THE SILENT STAR
arcs.blurb: A catalogued star that has always emitted a faint periodic radio pulse has fallen silent.

object.name: DS-1 (the silent star)
object.classification: Star with an unexplained radio cut-off
object.characteristics: FICTIONAL. A star whose periodic radio emission ended abruptly.

points.natural: A faint, repeatable change in the star's radio emission fits what is known about a stellar magnetic cycle ending.

points.natural: A second look confirms the change and its slow drift, consistent with a stellar magnetic cycle ending.
points.interference: The second dataset shows the feature moving with the station's own cycles, not with the sky.

points.artificial: The pattern repeats on a fixed cycle and carries structure that survives re-analysis: a pulse train that stops and restarts on a 3.1-hour schedule.

points.natural: The source region shows an ordinary physical environment, consistent with a stellar magnetic cycle ending.
points.interference: No source is found at the position; the signal came from within the Solar System's own transmissions.
points.instrumental: On-site instruments see nothing at all. The earlier detections were produced by the detector chain.
points.unknown: On-site measurements find a real source, but its nature cannot be classified with current knowledge.
points.artificial: On-site measurements find a compact source whose behaviour is hard to explain without design: a pulse train that stops and restarts on a 3.1-hour schedule.
